classification.difficultyReason: Evaluate the two branch expressions at the stated joining point, compare them with the defined value, and replace that isolated value with their common value.

children.label: a
children.prompt:
Show that the function $h(x)$ below is discontinuous at $x=1$.
$$h(x)=\begin{cases}2^x,&\text{for }x<1,\\4,&\text{for }x=1,\\3-x,&\text{for }x>1.\end{cases}$$

answer.short: $h(1)=4$, but the left-hand branch approaches $2$. Hence $h$ is discontinuous at $x=1$.
answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}h(1)&=4\\\text{Left-hand branch at }x=1&=2^1=2\\\text{Right-hand branch at }x=1&=3-1=2\end{align*}$$
Both branches approach $2$, which differs from $h(1)=4$. Hence $h$ is discontinuous at $x=1$.

children.label: b
children.prompt: What simple change to $h(x)$ would make it continuous?

answer.worked: Both branches approach $2$ at $x=1$, so set $h(1)=2$ and keep the other branches unchanged.
